title: Local group aids Black students under back-to-school stress - NewsBreak
text: BATON ROUGE, La. (Louisiana First) — Back-to-school can bring excitement, but also pressure, especially for some students in the Black community. A local group is guiding the youth before things take a dangerous turn. “There are unique challenges that young African Americans face,” said Michael Victorian. Challenges something so many in our area know well. “Dealing with peer pressure, whether that’s feeling isolated in their communities,” said Victorian. In those communities, heroes step in to change the narratives; Victorian is one. “We want to make sure that we are bringing that connectivity between adults and young people and making sure that young people know that they’re cared for,” he said. The 100 Black Men of Baton Rouge focuses on empowering young black men. Their goal is to step in early with guidance, resources, and support before it’s too late. “One of the greatest opportunities to address mental health challenges and suicide prevention is to make sure that young people stay connected and that they know that there’s somebody who’s standing in the gap to care for them,” he said. Mental health talks, mentoring sessions, and back-to-school outreach remind students that they always have someone to lean on, making 100 Black Men the first line of defense. “That’s the first layer of care, right?” said Victorian. “To make sure that young people understand that there are people, they have a community. I think that one of the greatest challenges related to mental health is folks feeling isolated.” That isolation is what Victorian focused on as school starts back. But the group doesn’t just focus on the classroom; it’s much more than that. “Whether it’s schools, school systems, churches, teams, coaches, we want to make sure that those young people know that they are connected to somebody and to something that cares about them,” said Victorian. Something Victorian said makes Baton Rouge special. For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to Louisiana First News.
